17use crate::{
18    common::{BitMatrix, Result},
19    Exceptions, PointCallback,
20};
21
22use super::AlignmentPattern;
23
24/**
25 * <p>This class attempts to find alignment patterns in a QR Code. Alignment patterns look like finder
26 * patterns but are smaller and appear at regular intervals throughout the image.</p>
27 *
28 * <p>At the moment this only looks for the bottom-right alignment pattern.</p>
29 *
30 * <p>This is mostly a simplified copy of {@link FinderPatternFinder}. It is copied,
31 * pasted and stripped down here for maximum performance but does unfortunately duplicate
32 * some code.</p>
33 *
34 * <p>This class is thread-safe but not reentrant. Each thread must allocate its own object.</p>
35 *
36 * @author Sean Owen
37 */
38pub struct AlignmentPatternFinder<'a> {
39    image: &'a BitMatrix,
40    possibleCenters: Vec<AlignmentPattern>,
41    startX: u32,
42    startY: u32,
43    width: u32,
44    height: u32,
45    moduleSize: f32,
46    resultPointCallback: Option<PointCallback>,
47}
48
49impl<'a> AlignmentPatternFinder<'a> {
50    /**
51     * <p>Creates a finder that will look in a portion of the whole image.</p>
52     *
53     * @param image image to search
54     * @param startX left column from which to start searching
55     * @param startY top row from which to start searching
56     * @param width width of region to search
57     * @param height height of region to search
58     * @param moduleSize estimated module size so far
59     */
60    pub fn new(
61        image: &'a BitMatrix,
62        startX: u32,
63        startY: u32,
64        width: u32,
65        height: u32,
66        moduleSize: f32,
67        resultPointCallback: Option<PointCallback>,
68    ) -> Self {
69        Self {
70            image,
71            possibleCenters: Vec::with_capacity(5),
72            startX,
73            startY,
74            width,
75            height,
76            moduleSize,
77            resultPointCallback,
78        }
79    }
80
81    /**
82     * <p>This method attempts to find the bottom-right alignment pattern in the image. It is a bit messy since
83     * it's pretty performance-critical and so is written to be fast foremost.</p>
84     *
85     * @return {@link AlignmentPattern} if found
86     * @throws NotFoundException if not found
87     */
88    pub fn find(&mut self) -> Result<AlignmentPattern> {
89        let startX = self.startX;
90        let height = self.height;
91        let maxJ = startX + self.width;
92        let middleI = self.startY + (height / 2);
93        // We are looking for black/white/black modules in 1:1:1 ratio;
94        // this tracks the number of black/white/black modules seen so far
95        let mut stateCount = [0u32; 3];
96        for iGen in 0..height {
97            // Search from middle outwards
98            let i = (middleI as i32
99                + (if (iGen & 0x01) == 0 {
100                    (iGen as i32 + 1) / 2
101                } else {
102                    -((iGen as i32 + 1) / 2)
103                })) as u32;
104
105            stateCount.fill(0);
106
107            let mut j = startX;
108            // Burn off leading white pixels before anything else; if we start in the middle of
109            // a white run, it doesn't make sense to count its length, since we don't know if the
110            // white run continued to the left of the start point
111            while j < maxJ && !self.image.get(j, i) {
112                j += 1;
113            }
114            let mut currentState = 0;
115            while j < maxJ {
116                if self.image.get(j, i) {
117                    // Black pixel
118                    if currentState == 1 {
119                        // Counting black pixels
120                        stateCount[1] += 1;
121                    } else {
122                        // Counting white pixels
123                        if currentState == 2 {
124                            // A winner?
125                            if self.foundPatternCross(&stateCount) {
126                                // Yes
127                                if let Some(confirmed) =
128                                    self.handlePossibleCenter(&stateCount, i, j)
129                                {
130                                    return Ok(confirmed);
131                                }
132                            }
133                            stateCount[0] = stateCount[2];
134                            stateCount[1] = 1;
135                            stateCount[2] = 0;
136                            currentState = 1;
137                        } else {
138                            currentState += 1;
139                            stateCount[currentState] += 1;
140                        }
141                    }
142                } else {
143                    // White pixel
144                    if currentState == 1 {
145                        // Counting black pixels
146                        currentState += 1;
147                    }
148                    stateCount[currentState] += 1;
149                }
150                j += 1;
151            }
152            if self.foundPatternCross(&stateCount) {
153                if let Some(confirmed) = self.handlePossibleCenter(&stateCount, i, maxJ) {
154                    return Ok(confirmed);
155                }
156            }
157        }
158
159        // Hmm, nothing we saw was observed and confirmed twice. If we had
160        // any guess at all, return it.
161        if !self.possibleCenters.is_empty() {
162            Ok(*(self
163                .possibleCenters
164                .first()
165                .ok_or(Exceptions::INDEX_OUT_OF_BOUNDS))?)
166        } else {
167            Err(Exceptions::NOT_FOUND)
168        }
169    }
170
171    /**
172     * Given a count of black/white/black pixels just seen and an end position,
173     * figures the location of the center of this black/white/black run.
174     */
175    #[inline]
176    fn centerFromEnd(stateCount: &[u32], end: u32) -> f32 {
177        (end as f32 - stateCount[2] as f32) - stateCount[1] as f32 / 2.0
178    }
179
180    /**
181     * @param stateCount count of black/white/black pixels just read
182     * @return true iff the proportions of the counts is close enough to the 1/1/1 ratios
183     *         used by alignment patterns to be considered a match
184     */
185    fn foundPatternCross(&self, stateCount: &[u32]) -> bool {
186        let moduleSize = self.moduleSize;
187        let maxVariance = moduleSize / 2.0;
188        for state in stateCount.iter().take(3) {
189            if (moduleSize - *state as f32).abs() >= maxVariance {
190                return false;
191            }
192        }
193        true
194    }
195
196    /**
197     * <p>After a horizontal scan finds a potential alignment pattern, this method
198     * "cross-checks" by scanning down vertically through the center of the possible
199     * alignment pattern to see if the same proportion is detected.</p>
200     *
201     * @param startI row where an alignment pattern was detected
202     * @param centerJ center of the section that appears to cross an alignment pattern
203     * @param maxCount maximum reasonable number of modules that should be
204     * observed in any reading state, based on the results of the horizontal scan
205     * @return vertical center of alignment pattern, or {@link Float#NaN} if not found
206     */
207    fn crossCheckVertical(
208        &self,
209        startI: u32,
210        centerJ: u32,
211        maxCount: u32,
212        originalStateCountTotal: u32,
213    ) -> f32 {
214        let image = &self.image;
215
216        let maxI = image.getHeight();
217        let mut crossCheckStateCount = [0u32; 3];
218
219        // Start counting up from center
220        let mut i = startI as i32;
221        while i >= 0 && image.get(centerJ, i as u32) && crossCheckStateCount[1] <= maxCount {
222            crossCheckStateCount[1] += 1;
223            i -= 1;
224        }
225        // If already too many modules in this state or ran off the edge:
226        if i < 0 || crossCheckStateCount[1] > maxCount {
227            return f32::NAN;
228        }
229        while i >= 0 && !image.get(centerJ, i as u32) && crossCheckStateCount[0] <= maxCount {
230            crossCheckStateCount[0] += 1;
231            i -= 1;
232        }
233        if crossCheckStateCount[0] > maxCount {
234            return f32::NAN;
235        }
236
237        // Now also count down from center
238        i = startI as i32 + 1;
239        while i < maxI as i32 && image.get(centerJ, i as u32) && crossCheckStateCount[1] <= maxCount
240        {
241            crossCheckStateCount[1] += 1;
242            i += 1;
243        }
244        if i == maxI as i32 || crossCheckStateCount[1] > maxCount {
245            return f32::NAN;
246        }
247        while i < maxI as i32
248            && !image.get(centerJ, i as u32)
249            && crossCheckStateCount[2] <= maxCount
250        {
251            crossCheckStateCount[2] += 1;
252            i += 1;
253        }
254        if crossCheckStateCount[2] > maxCount {
255            return f32::NAN;
256        }
257
258        let stateCountTotal =
259            crossCheckStateCount[0] + crossCheckStateCount[1] + crossCheckStateCount[2];
260        if 5 * (stateCountTotal as i64 - originalStateCountTotal as i64).unsigned_abs() as u32
261            >= 2 * originalStateCountTotal
262        {
263            return f32::NAN;
264        }
265
266        if self.foundPatternCross(&crossCheckStateCount) {
267            Self::centerFromEnd(&crossCheckStateCount, i as u32)
268        } else {
269            f32::NAN
270        }
271    }
272
273    /**
274     * <p>This is called when a horizontal scan finds a possible alignment pattern. It will
275     * cross check with a vertical scan, and if successful, will see if this pattern had been
276     * found on a previous horizontal scan. If so, we consider it confirmed and conclude we have
277     * found the alignment pattern.</p>
278     *
279     * @param stateCount reading state module counts from horizontal scan
280     * @param i row where alignment pattern may be found
281     * @param j end of possible alignment pattern in row
282     * @return {@link AlignmentPattern} if we have found the same pattern twice, or null if not
283     */
284    fn handlePossibleCenter(
285        &mut self,
286        stateCount: &[u32],
287        i: u32,
288        j: u32,
289    ) -> Option<AlignmentPattern> {
290        let stateCountTotal = stateCount[0] + stateCount[1] + stateCount[2];
291        let centerJ = Self::centerFromEnd(stateCount, j);
292        let centerI = self.crossCheckVertical(
293            i,
294            centerJ.floor() as u32,
295            2 * stateCount[1],
296            stateCountTotal,
297        );
298
299        if !centerI.is_nan() {
300            let estimatedModuleSize = (stateCount[0] + stateCount[1] + stateCount[2]) as f32 / 3.0;
301            for center in &self.possibleCenters {
302                // Look for about the same center and module size:
303                if center.aboutEquals(estimatedModuleSize, centerI, centerJ) {
304                    return Some(center.combineEstimate(centerI, centerJ, estimatedModuleSize));
305                }
306            }
307            // Hadn't found this before; save it
308            let point = AlignmentPattern::new(centerJ, centerI, estimatedModuleSize);
309            if let Some(rpc) = self.resultPointCallback.clone() {
310                rpc((&point).into());
311            }
312
313            self.possibleCenters.push(point);
314        }
315
316        None
317    }
318}
